analysis.title: Nasdaq Futures: Memory Meltdown
key_insights: GS's Memory and AI Semiconductor baskets fell 9.3% and 6.7% during October 5th-12th, creating headwinds for Nasdaq. Nasdaq lost 1.3% versus S&P +0.4% over the period.
Chinese memory chip maker CXMT reported "key progress" on a new cell architecture to boost memory density, presenting competition for SK Hynix.

Leveraged Nasdaq positioning initially appeared unconcerned before pivoting. Nasdaq 3 month funding versus Fed Funds richened, but Nasdaq's premium to S&P reversed from its local peak, particularly alongside index price weakness on October 12th.

In Commitment of Traders data, Other gross longs on October 6th were at 1 year highs in notional terms and as a percentage of open interest. Short-term correlations of this category versus Memory and AI Semiconductors were positive, so the category potentially reduced recently implemented length.

Asset Manager gross longs on October 6th did not show a significant relationship with either Memory or AI Semiconductors, so whether the Other category's behavior affects Asset Manager sentiment remains debatable.

sector_views.rationale: The sector traded poorly over the past week, with the GS Memory basket down 9.3% and the AI Semiconductor basket down 6.7%, weighing on Nasdaq.

risk_factors: Competition from CXMT's new memory cell architecture for SK Hynix.
Possible reduction of recently added Other category length in Nasdaq futures, given positive short-term correlations with weak Memory and AI Semiconductor baskets.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq 3 month funding versus Fed Funds richened, which the note reads as leveraged Nasdaq positioning initially appearing unconcerned.
Nasdaq's premium to S&P in 3 month funding reversed from its local peak, particularly alongside index price weakness on October 12th.
CFTC Commitment of Traders: Other gross longs in Nasdaq futures on October 6th were at 1 year highs in notional terms and as a percentage of open interest.
Asset Manager gross longs in Nasdaq futures on October 6th showed no significant relationship with Memory or AI Semiconductor performance.
